svg.title: The flow-volume loop and the volume-time curve from one forced breath
svg.desc: Left: a flow-volume loop with flow on the vertical axis and volume breathed out on the horizontal axis. The expiratory limb above zero rises to peak expiratory flow (PEF) just after full lungs (total lung capacity) and falls in a near-straight line to zero at residual volume; its width is the forced vital capacity (FVC). The inspiratory limb below zero is a rounded bowl back to full lungs, with peak inspiratory flow at its lowest point. Right: the volume-time curve of the same blow, rising steeply, passing FEV1 at 1 second and levelling off at a plateau equal to FVC; time zero is found by back-extrapolating the steepest part of the curve.

g.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, Segoe UI, Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
g.text: flow falls as the lungs empty
